Are you trying to win the Mega Millions, but your numbers never seem to come up? It may be time to look for better ways to make money. Fortunately, you can earn extra cash without going and getting a “real job.”.

What are the best ways to avoid sitting in a cubicle all day? Some money-making strategies require an upfront investment, while others let you earn money in your free time with the help of apps.

Read on to learn the best ways to earn cash without a regular 9-5 job, plus tips on how almost anyone can get started.

One of the easiest ways to earn money is by signing up to participate in market research studies. You won’t make much, a few dollars here and there, but you can create a free account and get started within minutes.

You’ll be paid in PayPal cash or gift cards for sharing your opinion and completing other tasks online.

According to recent reports, E-Poll Market Research is one of the top companies to consider for this type of work. They make it easy to create an account and answer survey questions.

However, there are plenty of other options to consider, including:.

While market research gigs won’t make you rich, it’s something you can do during your spare time.

If you have a book idea, turning your story into an eBook can help you earn passive income without a regular job. Kindle Direct Publishing can even help you format your book for Kindle, at which point you can market and sell your book to millions of potential readers who shop on Amazon.com.

How much can you earn writing eBooks? That depends on how many books you write, how much you sell them for, and how successful you are at marketing your book. Selling 20 books per month with a profit of $7 per book would net you $140 per month and $1,680 per year.

Meanwhile, selling 100 books per month at $7 per book would net you $700 per month and $8,400 per year. Need a little inspiration? Here’s an article that shows you how to make your first $1,000 selling eBooks.

You can earn a lot of money by starting a blog or niche website and monetizing it. I should know. I started Good Financial Cents more than a decade ago, and have earned millions of dollars through the monetization of this site since its earliest days.

How do you make money blogging? Earning real income with a website isn’t as easy as it looks, but there are plenty of monetization strategies you can try.

Here are the most common ways blogs make money:.

If you’re curious about what it takes to earn money blogging, consider signing up for my Make 1K Challenge. It’s free and can help you earn your first $1,000 online with some of the blog monetization strategies I’ve already mentioned.

You could argue that freelance work is like a regular job, but working at home and on your terms is much different from traditional employment. The fact is, most freelancers are fully remote – they can work from anywhere in the world with a laptop and an internet connection.

According to recent reports, plus, they can hire and fire clients based on their personal needs and preferences, and their income potential is unlimited. According to ZipRecruiter, freelancers in the U.S. average $63.53 per hour.

Of course, you’ll need a marketable skill to find paid work as a freelancer. This could be freelance writing, design skills, marketing expertise, or something else.

You can use several websites to market your skills as a freelancer, including:.

In a recent development, healthyWage makes it possible to earn money while you lose weight. You won’t earn a ton of cash through the app, but you can earn a few dollars and use it to supplement other income you have.

The more weight you lose, the more money you can make. For example, the HealthyWage website claims some of their clients who lost more than 100 pounds managed to earn anywhere from $1,400 to $3,000.

However, the HW weight loss calculator shows potential earnings of $578 to $828 for people who only have 15 pounds to lose.

If you have a car you rarely use and want to earn some side income, you can consider renting it out with Turo, a ride-sharing platform that connects car owners with people who need a short-term rental. You can set your price, although you’ll have more success if you price your car competitively.

Nicer vehicles in high-demand areas can easily fetch rates that surpass $100 per day through this platform. Turo notes that in-demand cars rented out regularly can bring in anywhere from $10,000 to $20,000 per year in net profit.

Plus, almost anyone can rent out their car provided it meets the guidelines of the Turo platform. Your car must be 12 years old or newer with less than 130,000 miles. It must be worth less than $200,000 (no Lambo’s), and you must also meet Turo’s auto insurance requirements.

Do you have a spare bedroom in your home that you never use? Maybe you have a basement or garage apartment you could fix up and begin renting for a profit?

Either way, Airbnb lets you rent out rooms and other spaces in your home on any dates you prefer. You must let renters know they’re renting a room in a home vs. an entire apartment or house and provide as much additional detail as possible.

The amount you can earn will depend on where you live and the type of accommodation you can offer. However, expensive cities like Chicago, Fresh York, and San Francisco have plenty of rooms for rent that go for well over $100 per night.

You may not have an entire room you can rent, but even if you have some storage space, Neighbor.com allows you to rent it out to others in need.

Common spaces rented through this platform include.

The Neighbor.com platform makes it easy to advertise your unused space so that people nearby can inquire if they’re interested. Also, note that the platform offers insurance that can protect you if some of your client’s items are damaged or stolen while in your care.

Sources indicate that how much can you make renting out extra space? It depends on how much space you have to rent and where it’s located. However, Neighbor.com reveals a range of rental space options that cost anywhere from $20 to $100+ per month.

According to recent reports, investing in dividend stocks is one of the best ways to earn money without a regular job. Many early retirees find a way to live and pay bills based solely on the dividends they receive from various stocks.

It has been revealed that but what exactly is a dividend stock? For the most part, they are regular stocks but with a track record of sharing their profits with investors through dividends.

Dividends can also be earned in exchange-traded funds (ETFs) or mutual funds, and they can be significant once you build up a large portfolio.

According to recent reports, since dividends are paid by profitable companies, they tend to be seen as less risky for investors. If you’re curious about what it takes to get started with this strategy, this post explains how to invest in dividend stocks.

It has been revealed that housesitting is an option if you’re somewhat mobile and can move from place to place. Generally, you can find house-sitting gigs through word of mouth, referrals, or online portals like Craigslist.org or Facebook Marketplace.

According to recent reports, that noted, not all house-sitting gigs are paid. Some offer the potential for exotic travel instead and free lodging for a week to several months.

Either way, a website called TrustedHousesitters is the best place to find house-sitting gigs. Some jobs posted are for house-sitting only, while others require house sitters to provide basic care for pets or plants.

If you have serious wanderlust and want to travel far and wide, this platform can help make it happen. Many gigs posted online are in countries like Australia, Ireland, France, and Switzerland.

If you love animals and want to earn money taking care of them, several platforms can help turn your dream into a reality.

Recent findings suggest that for example, Rover.com lets you provide basic care for dogs or cats in your home, or you can pick up dog walking gigs. Another mobile app, called Wag!, lets you do more of the same.

You can set your rates for all types of work through these platforms, and your availability. While earnings vary by location and job, most people watch dogs and cats for anywhere from $40 to $100 per night.

According to recent reports, real estate investing may seem like a pipe dream if you hope to earn income without a job but hear me out. There are many ways to earn income through real estate without owning physical property or dealing with the hassles of being a landlord.

Sources indicate that you can invest in real estate investment trusts (REITs) that let you build wealth over time. You can also use a platform called Fundrise to invest in real estate with a minimum investment of $10.

Fundrise lets you purchase eREITs, large investment funds that acquire, own, or operate multi-residential and commercial properties. The income you earn is entirely passive since it handles the work of finding income-producing properties and managing them.

It has been revealed that while returns are never guaranteed, Fundrise investors have achieved very solid returns. Investors who use the platform earned an average return of 7.31% in 2020, followed by 22.99% in 2021, 1.50% in 2022 and -7.45% in 2023 (their first down year).

You can earn income on your spare change by investing it using Acorns. The roundup savings app syncs to your debit or credit card rounds up every purchase you make to the nearest dollar, and invests the difference. Once it’s set up, there’s no work on your part.

According to recent reports, most of the money is invested in ETFs and managed by the world’s top investment firms like Vanguard and BlackRock. While this app makes it easy to invest small amounts of money, it’s not free to use. Personal plans start at $3 per month, while a family plan costs just $5.

If you’re looking for some paid gigs that are relatively easy, consider setting up a profile on TaskRabbit, an online platform that lets you get paid for completing various tasks, such as:.

Projects typically pay between $30 and $100, although some pay significantly more than that. TaskRabbit also lets you pick and choose the jobs you want to take on based on your availability so that you can work entirely on your schedule.

If you love taking photographs and have a knack for getting professional-looking images, you can use your skills and expertise to sell photos online.

Websites like Depositphotos and iStockPhoto pay photographers to supply them with stock photos they can sell to writers, publications, and various online platforms.

Sources indicate that the best part about this side hustle is that you can get started with the equipment you already have. While you can use a professional camera if you want to, many smartphones take professional-quality photos.

Earning a bank bonus is another way to earn money without a regular job, but you’ll need an upfront investment to get started. Most bonus offers require you to deposit a specific amount of money and keep it in your account for up to 12 months.

You may also be required to set up direct deposit to earn a bank bonus, and other terms and conditions may apply.

Recent findings suggest that where can you find the best bank bonuses? While bonus offers constantly change, you can start by checking with banks like Chase, HSBC, Radius Bank, and Wells Fargo.

Flipping furniture requires some upfront legwork and potentially even some artistic talent, but you can earn a solid income with this strategy if you know what you’re doing.

Essentially, this side hustle requires you to shop at thrift stores, garage sales, and online platforms to find furniture that will ultimately sell for more than you paid.

From there, you can sell the furniture as-is or clean it up and paint it with the goal of fetching an even higher price.

You can make money driving for Uber or Lyft on your own time, picking and choosing the days and hours you want to work.

Not only is rideshare work one of the most flexible side hustles, but you can earn $20 per hour and more with tips.

In a recent development, if you are low on free time but still want to make money without a job, consider selling stuff you don’t need. An array of online platforms makes it a breeze, although some platforms work better for selling.

For example, you can use Poshmark to earn money selling used clothing and accessories, while used electronics tend to sell best on platforms like eBay.com, Decluttr, BuyBackWorld, and Gazelle.

If you have home decor, furniture, or workout equipment to sell, you’ll almost always do better unloading those items locally on Facebook Marketplace.

Industry observers note that starting a YouTube channel is another way to earn money without a job, but that doesn’t mean it’s not work. The fact is, that creating quality videos and building an audience takes a lot of creativity and time. Plus, not everyone who tries to build a YouTube channel will succeed.

Industry observers note that that mentioned, you can earn income without a regular job. I know because I have done it with my YouTube channel, Wealth Hacker.

How much you can earn on YouTube varies quite a bit, but it’s possible to earn thousands of dollars per month. If you’re curious about monetizing videos, my in-depth guide will show you how to make money on YouTube.

When airlines raise transatlantic business class fares during summer holidays or major events, your points cost stays exactly the same. The gap between what the market charges and what LifeMiles charges simply grows wider. And then there's the no-fuel-surcharge policy — the detail that separates LifeMiles from competitors like British Airways Avios, which can pile $600+ in carrier surcharges onto a single redemption. Avianca is a Star Alliance member, which means it has reciprocal award booking agreements with every other Star Alliance carrier — United, Lufthansa, Swiss, ANA, EVA Air, Singapore Airlines, and more. Like all alliance programs, LifeMiles can sell award seats on partner airlines. The pricing is set by Avianca's own award chart, not by Lufthansa's chart or United's chart.

United MileagePlus charges 70,000–88,000 miles for the same seat. Avianca LifeMiles charges 63,000 miles with zero carrier surcharges. Same seat. Same plane. Wildly different cost.

Sources indicate that avianca keeps rates competitive because they want their program to be attractive to non-Avianca flyers — it's a revenue play. Personal Loan for a Renovation – Best When You’re Short on Equity or Time

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (430 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Use a personal loan for a small home project or an urgent repair, or when you have little home equity, since the money can arrive within days and your house isn’t collateral.
  • Borrowing against your home equity costs less than a personal loan because the house secures the loan, and that’s also why it’s slower and riskier.
  • A home equity loan or HELOC usually means an appraisal, closing costs such as title search fees, and a few weeks’ wait for the money.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Use a personal loan for a small home project or an urgent repair, or when you have little home equity, since the money can arrive within days and your house isn’t collateral. For a massive renovation, price a home equity loan or home equity line of credit (HELOC) first, which usually costs less.

Borrowing against your home equity costs less than a personal loan because the house secures the loan, and that’s also why it’s slower and riskier.

A home equity loan or HELOC usually means an appraisal, closing costs such as title search fees, and a few weeks’ wait for the money. Fall behind on it, and the lender can foreclose. A personal loan usually runs two to seven years, where an equity loan can run 20.

On a small job, the equity loan’s lower rate doesn’t save much. Say you borrow $15,000 for a bathroom remodel over five years, at 11% on a personal loan with no origination fee or at 8% on a home equity loan with $500 in closing costs. The personal loan’s interest comes to about $4,600 and the equity loan’s to about $3,200, so after its closing costs, the equity loan is only about $800 cheaper. On $50,000 at the same rates and term, the equity loan’s interest runs about $4,400 less than the personal loan’s before closing costs, which makes it worth pricing first for a significant renovation.

It has been revealed that before you apply, get your contractor’s written, fixed-price bid, so the amount you borrow matches a set price, not an estimate. Then rank personal loan offers by annual percentage rate (APR), not interest rate, since the APR includes the origination fee many lenders take out of the loan.

It has been revealed that take the shortest term whose payment fits your budget. At 11%, repaying $15,000 in three years instead of five raises the payment from about $326 to $491 and cuts the interest from about $4,600 to $2,700.

Compare the best personal loan companies, or see what you’d pay at the best home equity loan and HELOC rates.

It has been revealed that start with a free checking account for the money you spend and a high-yield savings account for the money you keep. Those two cover most people’s needs, so add a money market account or a certificate of deposit (CD), the other two types of bank accounts, only when a specific goal calls for one.

It has been revealed that savings left in checking earns next to nothing. Money for next month’s bills, locked in a CD, costs a penalty to pull out early.

In a recent development, all four are covered by FDIC insurance at an insured bank, or by similar federal insurance from the NCUA at a federally insured credit union, for at least $250,000 per depositor at each institution. They differ in how you reach the money, what it earns, and what it can cost.

Open a free checking account where your paycheck lands and a high-yield savings account for the money you’re keeping, at the same bank or two different ones.

In a recent development, add a money market account only if you want to write checks against a large cash balance, since high-yield savings often pays as much. A CD fits money you’ll need on a set date.

A newly introduced graduate, for instance, might open free checking at a bank with ATMs near home and high-yield savings at an online bank, then add a 12-month CD for a down payment she prepares to make in a year.

Look up a bank on the FDIC’s BankFind, or a credit union on the NCUA’s Credit Union Locator, to confirm it’s insured.

To pick your savings account, compare the best high-yield savings accounts.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that giving back a financed car leaves you owing whatever its sale doesn’t cover.
  • Those two numbers tell you whether a sale would pay off the whole loan.
  • Sources indicate that look up the car’s private-sale and trade-in values on Kelley Blue Book or Edmunds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that giving back a financed car leaves you owing whatever its sale doesn’t cover. To get out of a car loan, have a buyer, a fresh lender, or a dealer pay it off. Ask your lender for the payoff amount, compare it with what the car would sell for, and choose your exit before you miss a payment.

Those two numbers tell you whether a sale would pay off the whole loan. Your payoff amount can differ from the balance on your statement, since it includes interest up to the day you pay it off and any unpaid fees.

Sources indicate that look up the car’s private-sale and trade-in values on Kelley Blue Book or Edmunds. Say your payoff is $18,000 and the car sells privately for $19,500. The sale pays off the loan and leaves you $1,500. Add $7,500 of savings, and you can buy a $9,000 used car outright.

If the payoff is higher than what the car would sell for, you’re underwater on the loan, and closing that gap comes first.

Then take the first of these exits that fits:.

In a recent development, stopping payments costs the most. In many states, a lender can take the car without notice after a missed payment, sell it, and bill you for whatever the sale doesn’t cover plus its repossession costs. Having more than one type of debt is common, and that’s especially true once you graduate from college and start your first “real job.” You may have credit card debt, an auto loan, and a mortgage payment to make once you buy your first home. It’s also common to have other random debts to cover, including student loans.

Industry observers note that if you’re like many who took out loans during college, you will likely be paying them off after you graduate. In fact, 82% of students who borrowed loans expect to be making payments post-graduation, according to a recent College Ave Student Loans survey.

That noted, you’ll want to make sure you’re balancing debt repayment with your savings goals along the way.

In a recent development, you’ll also want to make sure you’re paying down debts in the optimal order, or in a way that will help you save the most money on interest as possible while aligning with your goals. Which debts should you pay off first? Here’s a rundown of how to get the best results:.

Industry observers note that no matter which types of debt you have, credit card debt should be your first priority. Why? Because credit card debt is likely the most expensive debt you have by far.

Federal Reserve data shows the average credit card interest rate on accounts assessed interest came in at around 22% as of May 2023, yet your credit card could easily be charging higher rates than the average.

To save as much money as possible, you should strive to pay as much as you can toward high-interest credit card bills each month. You can also pay down credit card debt faster with the help of a debt consolidation loan or a 0% APR balance transfer credit card.

It has been revealed that other unsecured debts like personal loan debt should come next in the debt payoff pecking order. After all, unsecured debts tend to have higher interest rates than secured debts like auto loans. In fact, the Federal Reserve also reported that the average interest rate on a 24-month personal loan came in at 11.48% as of May 2023, compared to the average rate of 7.81% on a 60-month auto loan.

Ideally, you’ll start paying more toward personal loan debt and other unsecured debts after all credit card debt is entirely paid off, although you should make at least the minimum payment on all your bills throughout the entire process.

The next debt you’ll want to tackle is your student loans. I suggest focusing on these loans after other unsecured debts, since federal student loans (and many private student loans) come with low fixed interest rates and monthly payments that will not change over time. If you have federal student loans, you may even want to look into income-driven repayment intends.

If you’re hoping to pay down student loans faster or just want to save money on interest, you can also consider refinancing your student loans to get a shorter repayment timeline, a lower monthly payment, or both. Just remember that refinancing federal student loans can mean losing access to income-driven repayment prepares and federal protections like deferment and forbearance.

Once you have paid off or substantially paid down all your other debts, you can focus your efforts on secured debts you have like mortgage loans and auto loans. These debts should be dealt with last since they are secured with collateral and tend to offer lower interest rates as a result. For example, you can consider paying more than the minimum on your mortgage, a car loan, or both until they’re paid off completely.

In a recent development, then again, you may want to pay off debts with extremely low interest rates as slowly as possible to free up more cash flow for living expenses and investments. If you took out a mortgage in January of 2021 when the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed rate home loan was as low as 2.65%, for example, it makes sense to make the minimum payment on that debt and invest your extra cash instead.

It has been revealed that it’s key to make sure you balance debt repayment with other financial considerations. After all, focusing too much on debt repayment early in life can leave you behind when it comes to investing for retirement or saving up for a first home.

While you’ll want to eliminate credit card debt and other high-interest debts as rapidly as you can, even if you have to stop saving and investing for a while, you can pay down student loan debt and secured debts at a slower pace while saving and investing for the future along the way.

Industry observers note that finally, make sure you have adequate emergency savings throughout your entire debt payoff journey, or that you begin saving for emergencies as soon as you can. Without a fully funded emergency fund, you can end up relying on credit cards and other loans to get by and ruin your debt payoff progress in the process.

How much should you save? While most experts recommend having an emergency fund that can cover three to six months of expenses, it’s okay to start small if you have to.

Having more than one type of debt is how it works for most people, especially when you’re young and in the early stages of your career. When it comes to paying it off, however, you’ll want to make sure you have a concrete blueprint that can help you reduce interest charges and get where you want to be.

Focusing on credit card debt and other unsecured debts first always makes sense, since these debts aren’t secured by an asset and tend to charge much higher interest rates. You can focus on student loans next, followed by other secured debts you have like a home loan or car loan.

In the meantime, make sure you have an adequate emergency fund and invest in it for retirement. After all, debt won’t last forever if you’re serious about repayment, and saving and investing early can help you benefit from compound interest and avoid using credit cards for surprise expenses. Creating a budget to track these factors is your best bet.

If you need help creating one, or simply don’t know where to start, use this budget worksheet as your guide – you’ll reach financial freedom in no time.

If a mistake on a tax return you already filed changes what you owe or get back, fix it with Form 1040-X. Amend within three years of filing to claim a refund, and pay any tax you owe when you amend, since interest runs until you pay. Skip it for math errors, which the IRS corrects itself.

Sources indicate that say you’re in the 22% tax bracket and forgot to deduct $1,500 of student loan interest. A 1040-X gets you 22% of that back, about $330.

Amend when the mistake changes your income, deductions, credits, dependents, or filing status. Two kinds of mistakes usually don’t need an amendment. Industry observers note that A refund has a deadline. You have three years after filing the original return to claim one, or two years after paying the tax if that gives you longer. It has been revealed that income you left off, such as freelance pay on a 1099 that arrived after you filed, means you owe more instead. The IRS charges interest on that tax from the April due date until you pay it, so amend and pay as soon as you can. Leave interest and penalties off the 1040-X, since the IRS figures them itself.

According to recent reports, if you’re expecting a refund on the original return, wait until that return has been processed. Then e-file the 1040-X through tax software that handles amended returns, including every form or schedule the change affects. E-filing works for recent tax years and lets you take any refund by direct deposit. Amend older years on paper.

Your state tax may change too, so check your state tax agency’s rules for correcting your state return.

Allow 8 to 12 weeks for the IRS to process your 1040-X, or up to 16 in some cases, and check its status in Where’s My Amended Return starting three weeks after you file.

#68094. How Unlimited Free Stuff from Amazon Almost Ruined My Retirement

How Unlimited Free Stuff from Amazon Almost Ruined My Retirement

📅 07 Oct 2025 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2051 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It all started last winter when I innocently posted a review for a heated vest I had bought on Amazon.
  • According to recent reports, “Congratulations!
  • I was already aware of Amazon Vine since I had seen product reviews from other people in the program – typically called “Vine Voices.” The basic idea of this program is that you can order stuff from Amazon for free, as long as you agree to review at least 80% of the things you order.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It all started last winter when I innocently posted a review for a heated vest I had bought on Amazon. I was happy with this fun upcoming way to beat the winter and wanted to share it with others, so I gave it five stars. But soon after I clicked “Submit”, I got an email from Amazon which said something like,.

According to recent reports, “Congratulations! You’ve been selected to join Amazon Vine for writing helpful reviews!”.

I was already aware of Amazon Vine since I had seen product reviews from other people in the program – typically called “Vine Voices.” The basic idea of this program is that you can order stuff from Amazon for free, as long as you agree to review at least 80% of the things you order.

“Hey, that’s cool”, I thought, “Who doesn’t like free stuff?

Especially since I’ve already been writing product reviews out of the goodness of my heart – why not be rewarded for it?”.

So without giving it much further thought, I clicked “accept” on their terms and conditions and joined the program.

And so began a saga that has taken me on a surprising journey over the past nine months causing me to:.

Industry observers note that okay, I’ll admit that there were also some upsides. My original idea was partly to save some money, by getting stuff I genuinely would have bought anyway, in a way that sounded fun. And that did happen – I saved at least a few thousand dollars on tools and materials for my construction business and the MMM-HQ Coworking space, for free. Plus, at least some of the motivation for signing up was to put myself through an experiment so I could write this blog article about it. And if you’re reading this, it looks like that happened too.

But I was still surprised at how powerful the combination of small nudges and incentives from Amazon was able to hijack my frugality instincts –  and get me to do a bunch of work that wasn’t really the best use of my time.

So I figured if we review my journey and break it down with a bit of Behavioral Science, we could all learn a few valuable things by laughing at Mr. Money Mustache’s folly.

Scarcity Brain and the Online Casino Effect.

One of the most interesting books I’ve read in recent years is Michael Easter’s Scarcity Brain. It’s an exploration of the sneaky ways that modern gambling platforms, marketing and social media algorithms are all built upon two weaknesses in our evolutionary programming:.

As I look back now, I realize that I fell straight into those same traps, because the Vine program has all the key properties of a casino or a TikTok feed:.

According to recent reports, but occasionally, there will be genuinely useful things like super nice light fixtures, tools and plumbing parts, an EV charger, and even some clothing. My favorite ridiculous Eagle shirt as featured in the Mustachianism music video was an Amazon Vine find.

As were a whole supply of super-realistic artificial plants, which while tacky in principle, have been amazing for hard-to-water courtyard garden areas at the MMM HQ.

In a recent development, I also had a lot of fun roping in friends and coworkers from HQ to help and share in the bounty. I let them help me request and review stuff that they wanted, and then they got to keep it. This seemed like a win/win because we shared the work and the fun of laughing at some of the ridiculous products available.

Still, as I went through this experiment this spring and summer and allowed the system to coax me into doing 80 reviews so I could upgrade my account from Vine Silver to Vine Gold*, I noticed something didn’t feel quite right.

Sources indicate that I was checking the Vine page every day for scores, even when I didn’t actually need anything. It would usually be a bust, but just often enough, something I actually wanted would come up, and I’d order it before it was too late. Scarcity and unpredictable rewards at work.

It has been revealed that then the bounty would come, I’d unpack it and photograph it with assembly-line speed so I could batch-write all the reviews once per week or so. For every review I did, I was spending time I’d rather spend doing something else. And for every questionable item I got, I was creating pollution and trash from its manufacturing and packaging – directly contradicting the main values of my life and my reason for writing this blog. And I saw all of this, yet I kept doing it!

So Was This The Downfall of MMM?

During the worst of this consumerism bender, things were dire. I was getting packages almost every day and my recycling bin was overflowing with cardboard. My son and my girlfriend started laughing at some of my more frivolous purchases, so I found myself discreetly tucking away the boxes when they were around to evade scrutiny.

According to recent reports, but eventually, I moved into a recovery stage. I had been letting this habit continue out of laziness and as a form of procrastination: it’s very easy to order shit online and pretend I’m doing something useful, and much more difficult to get moving to do the things that really make my life enjoyable.

But I’m old enough to know that hitting the running trails and the gym for my daily workouts, and making progress on all my construction projects, and focusing on the computer as a creative tool rather than an entertainment device so I can get stuff done like this blog post, are the things that bring me the most joy.

Recent findings suggest that admittedly, some of the sucky factors of the Vine program helped make it easier to recover too. For every genuinely useful thing I found like a contractor-grade extension cord, I had to scan through endless screens of trinkets which not only wasted my time but actually pissed me off at their very existence.

Industry observers note that I also noticed some of the deliberately reviewer-unfriendly features built into the program which reminded me that we reviewers are definitely just low-wage workers rather than any form of VIP. The search functionality is crap, and there is no way to filter or sort the results, because they want you to have to look through everything and they don’t care about the value of your time.

According to recent reports, then there is the hilariously bureaucratic AI-based evaluation system which would occasionally flag my totally tame, factual reviews as “Not meeting our Community Standards” without explaining what the problem was. So I’d have to go in and edit my review, randomly changing a couple of words and maybe some punctuation, and suddenly the AI would be pacified and accept my review. Just dumb.

This is What “Fuck You Money” is For!

According to recent reports, it dawned on me that for many people, this is just what “work” looks like. You are given a bunch of tasks and a bunch of rules to follow, in a system you didn’t create and don’t get much say in changing. And then as long as you crank out your TPS Reports without rocking the boat too much, you get your paycheck.

It reminded me of the Uber Driving experiment I did way back in 2017: as soon as I started working as a driver, I could immediately see dozens of improvements that could be made to the system that would make it function better for both drivers and passengers. But since I wasn’t the boss, nobody wanted to hear my ideas.

Experiences like these remind me that while I love hard work and I love learning new things every day, I greatly prefer being the boss. And I’ve gotten pretty damned accustomed to it after 20 years of financial independence, so I see no need to give it up.

Industry observers note that one interesting “gotcha” of the Vine program is that they do keep track of all the free stuff you get and send you a 1099 for its retail value at the end of the year. So it’s not really free, just discounted to whatever your marginal tax rate is (about 25% for me this year). If we peek into my account right now, this is how my 2025 is looking:.

So I got about $7000 worth of stuff, and could owe up to $1750 of tax on it. In my case, about 75% of it was “sold” to my business for commercial use (construction supplies which I used on jobs or HQ renovations) so it was effectively converted into real income rather than just tax burden. Some of it was stuff I would have bought anyway for my own house which I’ll gladly pay the taxes on. But there is also probably about $1000 of pure nonsense in there as well, for which I’ll owe a tax bill of $250 as penance for my itchy trigger finger on that “Order” button.

It has been revealed that thanks to some advice from wise readers in the comments (below), I have since learned that in most cases you can mark down this estimated value by 80% before declaring it – because you have effectively eliminated most of the resale value by opening and reviewing the product. Thus my tax bill will be more like $50 rather than $250. More detail in this Reddit discussion here.

In a recent development, so here we are today. While I admit that I didn’t explicitly cancel my account, I used the “Keystone Habit” trick to override the temptation to view the Vine page – mapping that browser bookmark to my daily habits list instead, a little chart which I call my “Badassity Tracker”. The net result is that every time I click it, I’m taken straight to a reminder to get up from the computer and do a quick round of exercise, so I do that instead.

And of course my writing of this article may be a violation of the terms and conditions of the program (“the first rule of Vine is to not talk about Vine”), so it might even get canceled on me. (and if so I’ll let you know because that would be funny story as well).

But I learned a lot about habits and addiction, and realized that this same feeling might be what drives people into One More Year Syndrome, as they keep working even when they can afford to quit. I have now coached enough people through this situation to see it is way more common than I would have ever guessed.

Industry observers note that as with all MMM articles, there’s a real life lesson in this story. It’s not really about Vine or me or my habits, it’s about you continuing to look at yourself and your life, and always questioning your own assumptions or patterns. And asking the people you trust most for feedback as well:.

According to recent reports, we will never be perfect, but the great news is we don’t have to be. All it takes is a little bit of self reflection and putting ourselves on a slightly better path, as often as we can as life goes on. We are all on a very long journey, so even a tiny course correction can make a huge difference in where we end up.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Missing a tax deadline can cost you a penalty, a refund, or a deduction, and the deadlines fall all year, from January’s estimated tax payment to October’s due date for extended returns. Add the dates that fit your income and accounts to your calendar as yearly reminders.

It has been revealed that income with no tax withheld, like freelance pay, can mean four estimated tax payments a year. An IRA or HSA adds an April deadline for last year’s contributions, and an extension moves your return’s due date to October.

Meeting one deadline doesn’t excuse missing another. A freelancer who files April’s return on time but skips the June 15 estimated payment can still owe an underpayment penalty on that payment. Last year’s total tax can tell you how much to pay on each date.

Sources indicate that A refund has a deadline too. If you’re owed one and don’t file, the IRS usually gives you three years to claim it, and after that the U.S. Treasury keeps the money.

These are the dates for individual filers:.

A date that falls on a weekend or legal holiday moves to the next business day. In 2027, January 31 is a Sunday, so employers and payers have until February 1.

The IRS also postpones deadlines automatically for people in a federally declared disaster area, and in 2020 it moved April 15 to July 15 for everyone because of COVID-19. Whenever a storm, flood, or fire hits your county, check the IRS’s disaster relief page to see whether your dates moved.

Set each date that applies to you to repeat every year in your phone’s calendar, with an alert a week ahead, starting with January 15.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, pack sandwiches and snacks from your kitchen and carry an empty water bottle to fill past security, since TSA lets solid food and empty bottles through the checkpoint. Spreads, yogurt, and drinks fall under the liquids rule, so each needs a container of 3.4 ounces or less.

According to recent reports, say an airport sandwich costs $13 and a bottle of water $4. That puts lunch for a family of four at $68, before snacks.

In a recent development, for a long day or a layover, pack food that keeps without a fridge. The USDA’s Food Safety and Inspection Service notes perishable food shouldn’t sit at room temperature more than two hours, or one hour above 90 degrees. Its list of foods that need no refrigeration includes bread, crackers, peanut butter, jelly, hard cheese, and whole fruit. For anything perishable, bring an ice pack frozen solid, since a slushy one counts as a liquid unless it’s cooling formula, breast milk, or baby food.

In a recent development, most fresh fruits and vegetables can’t come along on a flight to the mainland from Hawaii, Puerto Rico, or the U.S. Virgin Islands. The USDA bars almost all fresh fruits and vegetables brought into the U.S. from abroad, even ones handed out on the plane, and the EU bars meat and dairy brought from outside it. Finish those foods before landing, and declare what’s left at U.S. customs.

Sources indicate that when you do buy, choose a grab-and-go market over a sit-down restaurant, where a tip adds to the bill. Use any airport dining credit or lounge access your card already includes first.

Pack the night before: make the sandwiches, freeze the ice packs solid, and put the empty bottles in your carry-on.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the three-man Russian team returned to Everest’s West Ridge but found the route even more difficult than they expected. After two days of struggle, they’re heading back to Base Camp.

On October 20, Andrei Vasiliev, Serguey Kondrashkin, and Vitaly Shipilov went back up to the Lho La and pitched their tent on the wide plateau beyond. They still had time to fix more rope higher up.

“We moved…over terrain we’d already covered on the previous rotation,” the climbers texted to team member Natalya Belyankina, who had to abandon the expedition due to illness.

“The weather is good: sunny, with light winds, but cold,” they noted. “Progress was painfully slow today due to heavy packs and a persistent cough,” the climbers noted later.

In a recent development, on Wednesday, they hoped to reach 7,500m, spend the night there, check the route ahead, and then retreat to the plateau. However, they didn’t get as far as they had planned.

“We didn’t cover much ground today,” leader Andrei Vsiliev texted Anna Piunova of The Mountain Club. “The route is no walk in the park. We have to climb steep snowy slopes that conceal rock sections underneath.”.

To make things worse, they found no suitable bivy spots at their highest point, so they had to retreat to a place where they could pitch their tent for the night. Today, they were just too exhausted to keep going.

“We’re heading down; we’re sick and need to recover,” Vasiliev told Belyankina. “We can barely keep moving.”.

  • It has been revealed that say a contractor quotes $5,800 to tear out a 1990s tub and its tile surround and put in latest ones.
  • Recent findings suggest that reglazing coats the old tub and tile with a upcoming finish instead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A dated tub and tile are often sound under a worn finish. Before you pay to tear them out, check for wide cracks, leaks, and soft spots in the floor around them. Replace only what fails that check, and have the rest reglazed with a fresh coating for a fraction of what replacing them costs.

It has been revealed that say a contractor quotes $5,800 to tear out a 1990s tub and its tile surround and put in latest ones. If neither one is badly cracked, leaking, or soft underneath, most of that money replaces parts that still work.

Recent findings suggest that reglazing coats the old tub and tile with a upcoming finish instead. HomeGuide puts the price at $800 to $1,200 for a tub and the shower tile around it, so a $900 job would save $4,900 against that quote.

Sources indicate that the trade-off is lifespan. A reglaze lasts about 10 to 15 years, by HomeGuide’s estimate, and a second one when it wears out would bring your total to about $1,800, under a third of the quote.

According to recent reports, check the tub and walls first. Small cracks in a tub can be repaired for $100 to $300, by HomeGuide’s figures, but a wide crack, or a leak a plumber can’t fix, usually means a new tub. A soft spot in the floor or wall, or tiles that are loose or sound hollow when you tap them, point to water damage behind the surface. That section has to be torn out and repaired.

HomeGuide prices the rest of the refresh too:.

A reglazed surface needs gentle care. Wait at least 24 hours before using it, then clean it with a non-abrasive liquid cleaner instead of scouring powder or bleach, and use a bath mat without suction cups.

Get a reglazing quote for the same tub and tile before you sign a replacement contract, and put the difference toward whatever fails those checks.

Colorado Hiker Creates Ultimate Thru-Hike Across His Home State

📅 22 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1185 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, donovan Rice got into thru-hiking almost by accident.
  • Industry observers note that “I thought, there’s no way somebody can walk from Mexico to Canada.
  • Sources indicate that from there, it was a slippery slope.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, donovan Rice got into thru-hiking almost by accident. Already outdoorsy, he graduated from long hikes to planning to climb all 53 of Colorado’s 14,000’ers (mountains above 14,000 feet, or 4,267m). While researching which peaks required overnight camping, he realized that some people’s hikes just keep going.

Industry observers note that “I thought, there’s no way somebody can walk from Mexico to Canada. That’s just ridiculous,” Rice explained. “I fell in love with that idea.”.

Sources indicate that from there, it was a slippery slope. First came the Pacific Crest Trail (PCT), from the Mexican border in California to the Canadian border in British Columbia. Then he did the Continental Divide Trail (CDT), tracing the Rocky Mountains from Upcoming Mexico to the Montana-Canada border. Before he knew it, he had a trail name — Iceman —and was working the gig economy to free up time for wilderness adventures.

But that’s where most people’s slippery slope levels out. Hiking the 4,988km CDT is as meaty a project as most of us can imagine. But for Rice, it only opened the floodgates. He was fascinated by everything that didn’t make it into famous routes, especially the ridges and mountains he passed in his home state of Colorado that were just off trail.

Recent findings suggest that “There’s all this stuff the CDT doesn’t hit because it is following the Continental Divide,” he told ExplorersWeb. “So when I got to the end of the Colorado section, about 700 miles, I was thinking, man, if there were a 2,000-mile version of that, it would be my dream thru-hike. Just that non-stop, relentless brutality that is Colorado.”.

Sources indicate that colorado has 14,000′ peaks but also deserts. Photo: Donovan Rice.

Rice started thinking about a massive thru-hike loop of the state. His idea was to stitch together existing trails and form newly introduced ones where necessary.

“I dropped a load of pins across the areas in Colorado I wanted to visit, then I pulled out a public lands layer of the map to see how I might connect the areas,” he explained. “The three core design philosophies were beauty, breadth, and epicness. I wanted to see beautiful views, I wanted to cover as much of Colorado’s diversity as possible, and I wanted to take the most iconic and epic route possible.”.

Industry observers note that unlike places like the UK, there is no “right to roam” in Colorado, so connecting the route to avoid private land was tricky. Occasionally, he had to link bits of public land and sections of trail in the “least worst way,” with short road walks when private property appeared to halt progress.

Industry observers note that as he tacked on mountain peaks and the national parks he wanted to explore, his route swelled to a monstrous 3,000km+. His itinerary now included all 11 of Colorado’s national forests, three of its national parks, 13 14,000’ers and 47 13,000’ers.

In a recent development, “This is not an efficient route,” Rice admits. “You could walk the full perimeter of Colorado and then hike the Colorado Trail [an existing 885km trail from Waterton Canyon near Denver to Durango], and then still have kilometers left over [to complete the loop].”.

Sources indicate that the Great Colorado Route. Photo: Donovan Rice.

Industry observers note that the route looked epic on paper, but Rice still needed to prove it could actually be thru-hiked. After months of planning, Rice set off on his Great Colorado Route from Gunnison National Park on May 14, 2026. He traveled ultra-light, carrying just six kilos of gear, with just a quilt instead of a sleeping bag and a tarp rather than a tent.

Sources indicate that “I wanted it to be lightweight enough that I could be nimble on the mountains while doing these technical traverses,” said Rice. Traveling light was wise. Rice’s Great Colorado Route is challenging, with plenty of scrambling and sustained time at altitude.

Industry observers note that “The crux might be between Bailey and Rocky Mountain National Park. You go over the Mount Evans Wilderness, two 14,000’ers, hop on the Front Range across several 13,000’ers, and then across the Tenmile Range, and then the absolutely brutal Gore Range.”.

According to recent reports, rice spent 141 days tramping his trail, eventually finishing on October 1 after 3,252km. While he describes the route as “definitely not beginner-friendly” — due to plenty of cross-country terrain, off-trail navigation, and route-finding — it doesn’t require mountaineering skills.

“For me, the real sweet spot is Class three scrambling,” he states. “Once you get up to Class four, it starts getting really scary, and I had no tolerance at all for true Class five rock climbing.”.

In a recent development, however, he did pack an ice ax, micro-spikes, snow gaiters, and a lightweight helmet to protect against rockfall. He also made an effort to structure the route to provide relief between the most challenging sections, giving the trail an ebb and flow, and potential hikers time to decompress.

Sources indicate that the Ballard to La Junta traverse. Photo: Donovan Rice.

It has been revealed that overall, his focus on scenic beauty over contrived difficulty helped keep the route somewhat accessible. This is important because Rice hopes that other hikers will give it a go. He is building a website that maps the route, segment by segment, with GPS coordinates to help future hikers find the best places to camp or alternative paths depending on trail conditions. This is a May-through-October trail, but Rice stresses that it is unrealistic to expect perfect conditions for four and a half months.

According to recent reports, “This is one of those routes where bailouts will have to happen,” Rice explained. “You’ll have to take a low route or an alternate. I’m hoping to revisit some of the areas in the future and establish some of these alternative routes.”.

He aims to get all 29 segments of the initial route fully mapped on The Great Colorado website by the end of the year. It’s a major project, almost as big as the hike itself.

“I need to see how many people will actually give it a try. People can do segments. I’d love to see more thru-hikers do this, but the major challenge is that I think the majority of thru-hikers will look at this and think ‘that’s above my pay grade’.”.

Sources indicate that the Castles, Colorado. Photo: Donovan Rice.

Once he finishes the website, the level of interest might dictate his next steps. “I don’t know what level of formal recognition I want to try for. Do I want to try to get it codified? Or should it stay unofficial and remain just some cool thing someone did that published information on how to do it yourself.”.

Whether or not his Great Colorado Route ever gains the name recognition of the CDT or PCT, Rice has authored something unique, and in a world full of rehashes and copycats, that makes it special.

Rice looking down on Island Lake from Ulysses S. Grant Peak. Photo: Donovan Rice.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Buy TVs, laptops, tablets, small kitchen appliances, smart-home gear, and toys over Black Friday and Cyber Monday, when their deepest discounts land. Wait for January’s sales on treadmills and bedding, and check the price history of anything else on your list before you pay.

A Black Friday discount is worth taking only on something that won’t sell for less later in the year.

Price data from Consumer Reports (CR) indicates that 46 kinds of products it tests reach their lowest prices in November, among them TVs, laptops, tablets, air fryers, coffee makers, blenders, smart speakers, thermostats, and security cameras. CR expects Black Friday and Cyber Monday to bring the best deals of the year.

Sources indicate that adobe, which analyzes online sales at U.S. retailers, expects this holiday season’s best deals on TVs, toys, and appliances to land on Black Friday, and the deepest discounts on computers on Cyber Monday. It forecasts discounts of up to 30% off list price on electronics and 29% on toys. Sporting goods should see their best deals a day earlier, on Thanksgiving.

Fitness equipment and bedding are January buys instead. January’s sales are sparser overall, CR notes, but they tend to bring good prices on treadmills and other fitness equipment. Many stores also run white sales then, bedding promotions with substantial markdowns on sheets and pillows. So a laptop on your holiday list is worth buying on Cyber Monday, while a treadmill on the same list can wait for January.

Industry observers note that for anything else on your list, such as a sofa, look up its price history, which charts what the item has cost over recent months. Buy if the price sits at or near its recent low, and otherwise wait for the item’s own yearly sale season.

Before Thanksgiving, mark each item on your list as a Black Friday buy or a January buy, and set a price alert on the rest.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This morning, rescuers found the bodies of Japanese climbers Hidesuke Taneishi, 40, and Tetsu Hashimoto, 25, on Gangapurna West.

“Both bodies were found at around 6,300m on the south side of Gangapurna West,” the rescue team told The Tourism Times.

Industry observers note that hidesuke Taneishi (left) and Tetsu Hashimoto (right) with a support team member in Kathmandu earlier this week. Photo: Cosmo Adventure.

The climbers were attempting the first ascent of the 7,140m mountain and lost contact on October 15 at approximately 7,050m on their summit push.

A search-and-rescue team has been looking for the pair since October 19. Unfortunately, no one knew where they were on the mountain, or even if they were on the mountain at all. Therefore, the search started at Manang village, with no success.

The team included helicopter pilot Sobit Gauchan, high-altitude photographer and climber Manish Maharjan, and IFMGA mountain guide Pansang Rinzee Sherpa. The helicopter dropped Maharjan and Rinzee at 5,750m, and from there they used a drone to search the upper slopes. They scouted the northeast and southwest sides of the mountain, and finally found the remains of the Japanese climbers’ higher camp. Today, they found the bodies on the south side.

As for the cause of the accident, Rinzee told ExplorersWeb that their observations of the terrain pointed to a snow slab collapse.

According to recent reports, several teams have attempted Gangapurna West, located next to the Annapurna massif in Manang district, since it opened to foreign teams in 2014. However, none have summited. The mountain is also known as Asapurna or Lachenal Peak.

Team leader Hidesuke Taneishi was nominated for a Piolet d’Or last year after his first ascent of 6,652m Pholesobi Peak, also in Nepal, via a direct route up its vertiginous north face with Hiroki Yamamoto.

It has been revealed that hidesuke Taneishi on the summit of Pholesobi Peak. Photo: Hiroki Yamamoto.

Industry observers note that gross income is all income that isn’t exempt from tax. Wages, tips, taxable interest, and unemployment benefits count, and so does a home sale’s gain, even if you can exclude it from tax. Social Security benefits count only in part, and only once half of them plus your other income, tax-exempt interest included, passes $25,000, or $32,000 on a joint return. Married people filing separately who lived together during the year count that part at any income.

These require a return whatever your income:.

The IRS’s Interactive Tax Assistant asks about your filing status, withholding, and income, then notes whether you must file or should file for a refund.

Say you’re single, under 65, and earned $12,000 part time in 2026, with $700 of federal income tax withheld. You owe no income tax and don’t have to file, but only a return gets the $700 back. Refundable credits such as the Earned Income Tax Credit also pay out only to filers.

A return filed within three years of its due date still gets its withholding back, so a skipped 2023 return has until mid-April 2027.

In a recent development, every year, the Banff Centre Mountain Film and Book Festival celebrates the best mountain and adventure writing, film, and photography. The literary highlight of this alpine-themed celebration is the Banff Mountain Book Competition, with eight categories and one grand prize. The jury will award the grand prize at the festival, but the category winners have been declared.

Recent findings suggest that first, the two Special Jury Mentions. Jack Plant’s Spirit of the Great Bear showcases his spectacular photography of the Great Bear Forest. Meanwhile, Ian Nicholson’s Glacier Travel & Crevasse Rescue: Essential Skills for Snow Travel does exactly what it notes on the tin. “Of all the skill sets required for mountain climbing, perhaps none are as intimidating as glacier travel. But with carefully crafted instructions and illustrations, Nicholson takes us behind the curtain,” jury member Lauren DeLaunay Miller explains.

The Mountain Literature award went to Lone Wolf: Walking the Line Between Civilization and Wildness by Adam Weymouth. Weymouth dives into the place of wild animals in modern Europe, a continent “undergoing profound climatic, environmental, and political changes.”.

Black Bear: A Story of Siblinghood and Survival by Trina Moyles won the Environmental Literature category. “Black Bear seamlessly weaves together two complex storylines, laying bare Moyles’ relationships with her brother and with the wildlife she meets while working in a fire watch tower in Alberta.”.

Recent findings suggest that the Mountain Article prize, awarded to a magazine piece rather than a book, went to The Misfits by Chad Heddleston. Heddleston chose to profile rock climbing couple Jan and Herb Conn. “These two exist in the spirit and austerity of the pioneering European climbers of the early 20th century. The writing highlights their uniqueness and the integrity of their life choices,” jury member David Chambre said.

Pioneering rock climbers Jan and Herb Conn. Photo: Dwight Deal.

Industry observers note that the Adventure Travel prize went to North to the Future: An Offline Adventure through the Changing Wilds of Alaska by Ben Weissenbach. “Weissenbach — an L.A. native with little prior wilderness experience — treks through the Alaskan tundra with a series of eccentric environmental scientists and returns with a new perspective on technology and a revitalized sense of wonder for the natural world.”.

It has been revealed that cabin Wild: Alpine Bivouac Huts by Ben Tibbetts won the Guidebook award. “A captivating volume that invites us to see the Alps in a latest light, through an intimate journey around a selection of bivouac huts across Italy, Switzerland, and France,” according to jury member Rob Lovell.

The Mountain Image award went to Fjell: A Faithful Witness by Orsolya Haarberg. “A highly original book that takes us on a journey through the Norwegian highlands. It is as much an art book as a book about mountains,” explains jury member David Chambre.

Finally, The Great Mixed Climbs of Scotland by Guy Robertson & Hamish Frost won the Climbing Literature prize. “The Great Mixed Climbs of Scotland combines stunning photography and evocative essays in a truly spectacular ode to Scottish winter climbing. By profiling key routes through the eyes of the climbers who created them, Guy Robertson and Hamish Frost have created an exceptional book.”.

The category-winning authors get cash prizes and a chance to win the grand prize at the festival on November 5.

#68081. The Mountain That Looked Impossible: Muztagh Tower, 1956

📅 23 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1675 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Explorersweb ↗ Open Full Page

The Mountain That Looked Impossible: Muztagh Tower, 1956

📅 23 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1675 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that for nearly half a century, a single photograph defined one of the Karakoram’s most striking peaks.
  • Sources indicate that in the summer of 1956, two independent expeditions arrived on opposite sides of the peak, each convinced they were looking at one of the range’s last great unclimbed problems.
  • Recent findings suggest that vittorio Sella was born in 1859 in Biella, Italy, into a family connected to the mountains.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that for nearly half a century, a single photograph defined one of the Karakoram’s most striking peaks. Taken in 1909 and reproduced in books and journals, it showed Muztagh Tower as a vertical blade, a slender tooth of rock and ice rising from the glaciers with no obvious weakness. Generations of climbers studied it and concluded that the mountain was impossible to summit.

Sources indicate that in the summer of 1956, two independent expeditions arrived on opposite sides of the peak, each convinced they were looking at one of the range’s last great unclimbed problems. But the photograph had misled them.

Recent findings suggest that vittorio Sella was born in 1859 in Biella, Italy, into a family connected to the mountains. His uncle, Quintino Sella, had helped found the Club Alpino Italiano, and his father, Giuseppe Venanzio Sella, was a pioneer of early photography who published the first important Italian treatise on the subject.

In a recent development, vittorio Sella combined serious alpinism with large-format photography. He made the first winter ascent of the Matterhorn in 1882, followed by the first winter traverse of Mont Blanc. Throughout his career, he carried heavy glass-plate cameras into the high Alps, the Caucasus, Alaska, the Ruwenzori, and the Karakoram.

It has been revealed that sella’s photographic technique was excellent. His plates were large, the detail exceptional, and the compositions carefully chosen. His work was much admired, including by American photographer Ansel Adams. In a 1946 article for the Sierra Club Bulletin, Adams paid tribute to Sella’s work, writing:.

“The purity of Sella’s interpretations move the spectator to a religious awe. Sella has brought to us not only the facts and forms of far-off splendours of the world, but the essence of experience which finds a spiritual response in the inner recesses of our mind and heart.”.

Vittorio Sella. Photo: Alpine Club Photo Library.

Sella’s most notable Himalayan photographs came from the 1909 K2 expedition led by Luigi Amedeo, Duke of the Abruzzi.

Filippo De Filippi’s official account of the expedition, Karakoram and Western Himalaya 1909 (published in English in 1912), was illustrated throughout with Sella’s images. Those photographs remain among the finest early records of the range. One of them, a telephoto view of Muztagh Tower, became famous far beyond the expedition report, and inadvertently sparked a legendary mountaineering myth.

Muztagh Tower (7,276m) is located in the Baltoro Muztagh of the Karakoram, on the border between Pakistan’s Gilgit-Baltistan and China’s Xinjiang. It rises between the Baltoro and Sarpo Laggo Glaciers, just north of the main Baltoro corridor leading toward K2.

The peak has two summits only a short distance apart. The eastern peak is the true summit, and the western summit is a few metres lower. From most angles, the mountain is a substantial massif with steep but not uniformly vertical faces. From one particular viewpoint it collapses into something that looks far more extreme.

Sources indicate that muztagh Tower taken from the Upper Baltoro Glacier in 1919 by Vittorio Sella. The tower appears as an impregnable tooth. The photo inspired mountaineers for decades. Photo: Vittorio Sella.

Sources indicate that sella took the image of Muztagh Tower from the upper Baltoro Glacier, looking northwest toward the mountain. The twin summits lined up almost perfectly. The long telephoto lens compressed the intervening ground and presented the peak as a narrow, knife-edged tower whose walls appeared to fall nearly vertically from summit to glacier.

From other angles the peak revealed broader ridges and less precipitous slopes, but this single compressed view was the one that circulated widely. The effect was really dramatic, but as later climbers discovered, also misleading. In 1941, Sella’s photo of Muztagh Tower appeared in a mountaineering book under the caption “The Last Citadel.” The image fixed the mountain’s reputation for decades.

Recent findings suggest that muztagh Tower, 1909. Photo: Vittorio Sella.

In 1956, a British team and a French team both set out for Muztagh Tower, drawn in large part by Sella’s photograph.

The British team, led by John Hartog and consisting of Joe Brown, Ian McNaught-Davis, Tom Patey, and liaison officer Captain Riaz Mohammad, chose the Northwest Ridge. They planned to approach via the Muztagh and Chagaran glaciers on the western side of the peak.

The French party, led by Guido Magnone, included Andre Contamine, Paul Keller, Robert Paragot, Francois Florence, and liaison officer Ali Usman. They worked from the eastern side, aiming for what became the eastern arête after reconnaissance ruled out the North Ridge. The two groups operated independently on opposite flanks of the mountain.

The British established Base Camp on the Muztagh Glacier on May 28, 1956, at 4,282m. Through the first half of June, they placed camps on the Chagaran Glacier, avoiding the worst of the lower icefall by climbing the northern moraine and then threading seracs. Camp 3 was set on the west col at 6,355m after a steep ice wall. They reached the col on June 16, but took until the end of the month to move tents, fuel, and food up.

Industry observers note that from there the route followed the exposed crest of the West Ridge, a mixed line of rock, snow and ice that required fixed ropes on the steeper sections. Brown made a key traverse around a rock cliff on the South Face. Camp 4 was placed on the ridge itself at 6,439m.

According to recent reports, above the high camp, the climbing continued up a narrow couloir and then mixed ground. The final technical obstacle was a short rock leaf between the two summits, graded alpine V and exposed on both sides.

Industry observers note that on July 6, Brown and McNaught-Davis reached the western summit. The following day, Hartog and Patey, after supporting the first pair, crossed the connecting ridge and stood on the slightly higher eastern summit. Both pairs had to bivouac on the descent. Hartog suffered frostbitten toes. All four climbers reached the top.

Muztagh Tower. Photo: Hunza Adventure Tours.

Recent findings suggest that the French established their Base Camp at 4,496m on June 12 after approaching from the Younghusband Glacier. Their reconnaissance promptly revealed the North Ridge was impossible, so they moved onto the eastern branch of the glacier.

According to recent reports, they fixed ropes through an icefall and up a rock-and-ice spur, placing successive camps until Camp 4 stood at the foot of the summit pyramid at 6,300m. On July 6, as bad weather closed in, they spotted the British climbers moving on the upper heights.

Sources indicate that after the two-day storm cleared, the French regained the ridge, overcame two substantial rock towers, and bivouacked high on the mountain. On July 12, Magnone, Paragot, Contamine, and Keller reached the main summit through deep snow, six days after the British first topped out. After summiting, they descended to Camp 4 after dark. Dr. Florence had waited at high camp for more than 40 hours without radio contact during the summit push.

Recent findings suggest that the British party therefore made the first ascent of Muztagh Tower. The French completed an independent second ascent six days later. Both teams discovered that the mountain, while technically demanding and exposed, offered viable lines. The route, while serious, proved less relentlessly steep than Sella’s photograph had suggested.

In a recent development, the two expeditions were not engaged in a formal competition. They approached from opposite sides, followed separate routes, and maintained cordial relations. The British simply reached the summit first. The French, seeing the British already on top, continued their own line to completion.

Recent findings suggest that far from a bitter nationalistic race, the two teams demonstrated alpine solidarity. The French team chose the east side specifically to avoid interfering with British progress on the western side. Rather than abandoning their push in defeat after spotting the British on the summit, the French celebrated their colleagues’ historic achievement and resolutely pushed forward to fulfill their own objective. When Hartog suffered severe frostbite during his descent, the French team stepped in to provide vital assistance and support during the evacuation.

It has been revealed that the southeast side of Muztagh Tower, showing the route. Photo: Guido Magnone for The Himalayan Journal.

It has been revealed that since 1956, Muztagh Tower has remained one of the least visited major peaks in the Karakoram. A British team in 1984 repeated the Northwest Ridge (Mal Duff, Tony Brindle, Jon Tinker, and Sandy Allan), though they reached the slightly lower west summit rather than the true east summit. In 1990, a Swedish party consisting of Göran Kropp and Rafael Jensen also successfully scaled the Northwest Ridge.

In August 2008, Slovenian alpinists Pavle Kozjek and Dejan Miskovic made a groundbreaking alpine-style push up the steep Northeast Face. They successfully reached the upper ridge crest, but ferocious winds ended their push. Tragically, just after beginning their descent, a ridge cornice collapsed, and Kozjek fell to his death.

The 2,000m Northeast Spur of Muztagh Tower showing the line “Think Twice.” Photo: American Alpine Journal.

In a recent development, four years later, Russians Sergey Nilov, Dmitry Golovchenko, and Alexander Lange made the historic first ascent of the massive Northeast Spur. Their grueling 17-day climb via a new route named “Think Twice” reached the true summit, earning them the prestigious Piolets d’Or. The Russian team indicated in their expedition report that Muztagh Tower was 7,284m.

According to recent reports, the 1956 French route has never been fully repeated to the main peak, and no further ascents of the true summit have been confirmed since the 2012 Russian expedition. Still, climbers continue to push limits here, most notably in 2019, with the first ascent of the Black Tooth (6,718m), a difficult lower spire on the mountain’s ridge.

Muztagh Tower (top left) and its Southeast Ridge, with a high point on the Black Tooth (6,719m). The solid line, with the two marked bivouac sites, is the line of ascent to Black Tooth followed by Simon Messner and Martin Sieberer in 2019. Photo: Simon Messner/American Alpine Journal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a bathroom remodel, put your splurge into one feature you’ll see or touch every day, like the vanity top or showerhead, and buy budget versions of the other finishes. Don’t skimp on what the walls hide, like the waterproofing behind the tile and the valve behind the shower handle, since fixing either later means opening a finished wall.

In a recent development, A bathroom looks expensive because of what the eye lands on first, like a stone vanity top, a rainfall shower, or one wall of standout tile. Premium material on every other surface raises the bill without changing that first impression.

Choose the splurge by how often you’ll use it. You touch the vanity top and stand under the showerhead every day.

Everywhere else, these budget choices hold up:.

Sources indicate that one swap can pay for the splurge. Say a couple wants a $1,200 quartz vanity top, and their quote prices 120 square feet of marble tile at $15 a square foot, or $1,800 before labor. Porcelain that looks like marble, at $2 a square foot, costs $240 for the same space, a $1,560 saving that pays for the top with $360 left over. Refinishing a tub that’s still in good shape and shopping salvage stores cut the bill further.

In a recent development, don’t cut corners on three things. Tile and grout let water through, so the waterproofing membrane behind them keeps the wall dry, and a failed one means tearing out the fresh tile. Replacing the valve behind the shower handle later means opening the wall it’s in. And the EPA advises a working exhaust fan vented straight outside, not into the attic, to clear the moisture that lets mold grow.

Ask the contractor to name the membrane, valve, and fan by brand and model in the quote, so none gets downgraded to lower the total.

  • Industry observers note that with an entire river to descend, the film wastes no time getting right into it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This full-length adventure documentary follows kayaker Dane Jackson and a small team down Chile’s remote and wild Rio Cuervo.

Industry observers note that with an entire river to descend, the film wastes no time getting right into it. Dane Jackson introduces into the complicated business of trip logistics, trying to find a way to get the team and their equipment to the beginning of the river. Besides him, the team consists of the trip’s mastermind, Kilian Astorga, and kayakers Tom Dolle, Eirik Hansen, Adrian Mattern, and David Sodomka.

Forty years ago, there was a road up to Lake Mayuin, the volcanic pool from with Rio Cuervo flows. It’s gone now, so they turn to helicopter transport. With their gear dangling below on a rope, the chopper carries them up into the mountain, depositing kayaks and kayakers alike on the lakeshore. They set up camp and settle in to begin the first descent of the Rio Cuervo.

The team scouts the head of the river, swelled with recent rainfall. Photo: Screenshot.

It has been revealed that the dense forest and sometimes steep banks add another layer of difficulty as they begin to make their way downstream. They have to plan ahead, as there are stretches where it is impossible to bail if the rapids become too much. This means more portaging, which is painfully slow due to the thick vegetation.

When they do hit the rapids, on-board cameras capture the frenetic energy of whitewater kayaking. But the film makes no attempt to conceal the reality of a first descent. Much of their time is spent scouting ahead by drone, poring over satellite images, portaging, and standing about debating logistics.

According to recent reports, sunset arrives before the end of their portage. Camping in the jungle makes for an uncomfortable night. Photo: Screenshot.

Sources indicate that jackson and the rest of the crew soldier on, though, cracking nerdy jokes (the jungle is compared to both Dagobah and Fangorn Forest) and making the best of bad weather and rough camping. In the final few days, conditions improve, and they can spend more time on the water.

In a recent development, the contrast between their slow, grueling push forward and the wild speed on the river brings refreshing energy to the kayaking sections. When the river finally widens as they glide into the sea, it feels like a hard-won victory.

In a recent development, running a 3.5km gorge. Photo: Screenshot.

Sources indicate that early in the production of a certain musical, Broadway director Harold Prince attempted to ask Andrew Lloyd Weber what the deeper political allegory or social commentary was behind the composer’s feline opus. Weber famously took a long pause and replied: “Hal, this is just about cats.”.

This movie is about kayaking. Many outdoor adventure films use the genre, and the adventure story, to explore grand themes, and some do so successfully. But when they fall flat, is it more annoying than I can begin to express. For that reason, I deeply respect the clarity of purpose evinced by Dan Jackson and First Descent Rio Cuervo.
